articles.title: The Whisper Man Review
articles.summary: The Whisper Man premieres globally on Netflix on August 28. Tragedy. Fathers desperate for connection with their sons and failing to find it. A string of murders that left a town shaken and an eerie nursery rhyme in their wake. Minds, homes, and families haunted.
body: Based on the novel by Alex North, the film follows newly widowed crime novelist Tom Kennedy (Adam Scott), who is forced to reconcile with estranged father and retired detective Pete Willis (Robert De Niro) when his son Jake (Acston Luca Porto) goes missing. The kidnapping follows the pattern of a child abduction and murder spree that Willis solved when Tom was just a boy; the circumstances of Willis’ involvement with the crime and its perpetrator left the detective so traumatized that he ultimately abandoned his family.

The only person who might know who is behind these grisly acts — a butcher of innocents known as the Whisper Man — sits rotting in the jail cell where Willis put him. Desperate to find Jake and assigned to the case, Detective Amanda Beck (Michelle Monaghan) joins forces with Willis in a partnership that’s one of several contrivances meant to move the plot along. Unfortunately, that team doesn’t always track, and the circumstances surrounding the home that Tom rents are so full of wild coincidences that one is left utterly baffled.
points: The Whisper Man premieres globally on Netflix on August 28.

articles.title: GTA 6 NPCs Will Notice If You’re Carrying A Weapon In Public
articles.summary: In Rockstar Games' Grand Theft Auto franchise, players have been able to walk the streets while armed to the teeth without attracting attention from the non-player characters populating the world.
body: According to a GTA 6 preview in The New York Times, "a player in this one cannot whip out a shotgun or a rocket launcher and walk down the street without expecting the non-player characters to call the police."

As disclosed in Netflix's extended GTA 6 preview special, the game has restored the six-star Wanted level to the franchise. Presumably players will get into more trouble for firing a rocket launcher than simply holding one. But allowing the NPCs to behave more realistically to potential threats adds a new aspect that players will have to consider going forward.

Although the apparent vocal stylings of the game's male antihero, Jason, have been negatively received, players have praised GTA 6's ability to interact with dogs and its potentially complex love story between Jason and his co-lead, Lucia.

GameSpot has put together a comprehensive roundup of everything we learned from Netflix's GTA 6 preview. Among the highlights are the expanded map size and a Red Dead Redemption 2-like honor system that keeps track of how the players behave in the game.

articles.title: The X-Tech Executive Chair Aims to Upend Premium Models from Herman Miller, Steelcase at a Better Price
articles.summary: Editor's Note: This article is sponsored by X-Chair. X-Chair's "top of the line" office chair - the X-Tech Executive - retails for $1,845, although it's currently on sale for $1,384. That places this chair firmly in the super premium tier.
body: At first glance, the X-Tech Executive looks like a typical office chair. It's not gaudy like some of the racing-styled gaming chairs out there. This is actually X-Chair's roomiest chair, with a 22" seat width and up to 275 pound weight capacity. X-Chair states on its page that the chair is best suited for medium to large-framed people.

The seat is made of a supportive cooling memory foam that contours to your body. The seat and upper back section are upholstered in Brisa performance faux-leather fabric that's both breathable and easily washable. The lower back is made of a flexible mesh material which X-Chair calls "adaptive thermoregulating (ATR)".

In terms of ergonomics, the X-Tech Executive features a dynamic variable lumbar system. The lower back is disconnected from the rest of the chair and adjusts automatically based on your movement. That way, your back is supported no matter what position you might be in. This dynamic lumbar foregoes your need to manually adjust the settings.

articles.title: Stealing Cars In GTA 6 Is Probably More Complicated Than You Expected
articles.summary: Grand Theft Auto 6 is following a tradition that Rockstar previously leaned into with Red Dead Redemption 2: a focus on realism. In the case of GTA 6, that means things like filling your car with gas, working out to get (or stay) fit, and eating to stay energized.
body: Whereas in past games, you could just smash the window of any car to get inside and drive off with it, in GTA 6, how you commandeer a vehicle that doesn't belong to you will be based on what kind of car it is.

For older cars, you can smash the window just as you always have, but for a quieter approach, you can instead use a slim jim, a device you've maybe seen roadside assistance services use if you've ever locked yourself out of your own car. Doing it this way requires a short minigame using the control stick on your PlayStation 5 or Xbox controller. Once you get into such cars, you can hotwire them and drive off.

But that's just for older cars. For newer vehicles, including whatever GTA 6's inevitable parody Tesla analog will be, you'll not be able to use these methods. Instead, you'll need a key cloner, allowing you to perform something known as a "relay attack."

These devices mimic the electronic signal that newer cars' key fobs utilize, and in both the real world and in Rockstar's satirical funhouse mirror of Florida, they allow criminals to remotely break into your car without even setting off the alarm.

articles.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 Will Have No Microtransactions Or Generative AI
articles.summary: Grand Theft Auto VI. It's the most anticipated video game of the year, and possibly of all time. Netflix just aired a 27-minute extended trailer, and you've likely read multiple stories about it right here on this site since.
body: Speaking on the Kinda Funny Gamecast, Kinda Funny's Andy Cortez and Greg Miller revealed that they asked Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson about the potential for microtransactions in GTA, as well as the use of generative AI in its development. Both reported that the answer to both questions was simply "no."
"Can you use your own real-world money to buy things in the game? No monetization," Cortez said. "I asked point blank, 'is AI in the game?' No AI," Miller continued.

The lack of generative AI was also reported by The New York Times in its Grand Theft Auto VI feature posted earlier today. "Grand Theft Auto VI, Rockstar said, has well over 600,000 animations, compared with 55,000 animations in Grand Theft Auto V and 300,000 animations in Red Dead Redemption 2," the article said, which also confirmed that Rockstar "emphasized the new game’s human-made craft."
For more on Grand Theft Auto VI, check out our coverage on just how big the map will be, whether or not you can pet (or even scold) a dog, and the return of a six-star wanted system.

articles.title: The Biggest Action Thriller Epic of the Year Officially Arrives in 3 Weeks
articles.summary: Zach Cregger has become one of the hottest directors in Hollywood thanks to the success of 2022’s Barbarian and 2025’s Weapons. Drawing on his experience as a founding member of the comedy troupe The Whitest Kids U' Know, Cregger combines humor and horror in films with shocking twists.
body: Resident Evil arrives in theaters in three weeks. Cregger's latest project has a far higher budget and also big expectations, as he has the chance to redeem a beloved horror game series with a terrible cinematic track record. It’s a labor of love for the director, though the project is already dividing fans worried that 2026's Resident Evil film will feel like the work of an auteur rather than the franchise they love.

That’s because Cregger’s spin on Resident Evil won’t include any of the franchise’s protagonists. However, the director says he’s a huge fan of Capcom’s horror series and has packed the film with Easter eggs, even shifting the perspective of his camera work in a way reminiscent of Resident Evil Requiem. Even if you’ve been burned by previous Resident Evil films, here’s why you should give Cregger’s a try when it arrives in theaters on Sept. 18.

Cregger’s Resident Evil is a full reboot of the Resident Evil film franchise, which was last rebooted in 2021 with Resident Evil: Welcome to Raccoon City. That film was a critical and commercial flop. Thankfully you don’t need to watch it or any other movies before jumping in.

articles.title: GTA 6's map is so massive, you could fit two GTA 5s in it - and we know roughly how long it'll take to beat too
articles.summary: As part of its massive GTA 6 info blowout, Rockstar has been talking sizes - both of the map kind and length kind - confirming its latest open-world epic unfolds across a world that's twice as big as that of GTA 5, and should take around 80 hours to complete.
body: Rockstar's head of development Rob Nelson shared the map size news in a chat with YouTuber TGG, revealing just how huge GTA 6 's version of Vice City and the areas beyond it really are. Summarising those eye-catching numbers, TGG explained, "The map is twice the size of GTA 5's map, three times the size of Red Dead 2's map. Vice City itself is twice the size of Los Santos, and Vice City and its surrounding suburbs is 11 times bigger than Los Santos and its surrounds, which is, like, nuts, dude."

To date, Rockstar's various trailers and announcements have revealed six key locations across the state of Leonida, GTA's 6 Florida-inspired setting. There's Vice City itself, of course, alongside one-time tourist hotspot Port Gellhorn, the sunkissed archipelago of Leonida Keys, the Grassrivers swamps, Mount Kalaga National Park, and Ambrosia. And while there's almost certainly plenty more we don't know about yet, it's clearly a lot of map and a lot of stuff within.

articles.title: GTA 6 has more than 10 times the animations in GTA 5, and double the amount in Red Dead Redemption 2, Rockstar confirms
articles.summary: Everyone was expecting GTA 6 to be massive, sure, but comparing the amount of unique animations in the game to what was included in Rockstar Games ' previous work really puts things into perspective.
body: Fresh off the back of Netflix's GTA 6: An Extended Look premiere, a preview from New York Times revealed that the open-world maestros at Rockstar Games built a whopping 600,000 different animations to bring Leonidas to life - its people, its critters above and below sea level, its cars, and practically everything else that moves.

But that massive stat doesn't tell us much without some context, so let's zoom out. To compare Grand Theft Auto 6 to the already mammoth games that came before it, Rockstar developers told the publication that GTA 5 included a still impressive 55,000 animations and Red Dead Redemption 2 had an also almost unbelievable 300,000 animations.

Just in terms of animation work, GTA 6 is 10 times bigger than GTA 5 and double the size of Red Dead Redemption 2. Kind of astounding when you remember how wide GTA 5 felt back in 2013, with its seemingly endless moving parts clunking away.
